extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to establish the issue rather than dismiss it. The candidate demonstration is that k1 takes only six distinct values across twelve rows, each exactly twice, so if k1 were a source-item identifier then every unit in the `a` collection would enter the independence-assuming t-test twice, inflating the effective n from 6 to 12 and understating the variance of the test statistic — a textbook repeated-unit entry into a row-independent procedure. To demonstrate this issue class I need the antecedent 'k1 identifies a source item' to be established by the visible files. It is not: the task states in terms that admit no reading otherwise that k1 is an opaque code and that the task 'does not establish whether either code identifies a source item within either collection.' Supplying that antecedent would require me to infer intent from the mere shape of the code values, which is precisely the unstated-intention guessing the review forbids. I also probed two alternative routes to the same issue class and both fail: (a) a row-level duplication route — no row or cell is read twice; each row contributes exactly one value to `left` and one to `right`, and df=22.0 confirms 12 and 12; (b) a cross-arm route, i.e. the same unit appearing in both samples — the task states the two collections are disjoint, so `a` and `b` items are not the same units, and k2 is unique per row in any case. I checked the inverse error too (that a paired procedure was owed): the task states the row pairing is storage convention with no relationship, so ttest_ind is the matching choice and the report is not a mis-specified paired analysis. The verdict therefore survives falsification: the repetition is visible but its interpretation as repeated independent-unit entry is expressly not established, and the row-level entry that did occur is exactly what the task authorized. Residual risk is confined to the possibility that the visible k1 pattern was intended as an identifier despite the disclaimer, which I decline to assume.
